note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old woman with 3–4 days of constant, worsening midline lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain (≈8/10) associated with light pink vaginal spotting, slight discharge, and nausea without vomiting; last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago; sexually active; contraceptive implant in place for ~1 year; last pregnancy test ~1 month ago; advised to do pregnancy test today and attend face-to-face exam to evaluate for causes including ectopic pregnancy, PID, or ovarian cyst.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Constant lower abdominal pain, midline below the umbilicus; severity ~8/10; present at all times.
  - Associated light pink vaginal bleeding/spotting and small amount of vaginal discharge.
  - Nausea without vomiting.
- Timeline:
  - Pain began a few days ago and is getting worse.
  - LMP approximately 2–3 weeks ago; last period described as normal and then stopped; spotting since then is lighter and different in color.
  - Constipation last week for about a week; bowel habits improved this week.
  - Last sexual intercourse ~4 days ago.
  - Contraceptive implant inserted ~1 year ago; menses occur but are irregular on implant.
  - Last pregnancy test about 1 month ago (not since pain started).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not specified.
- Associated symptoms / ROS:
  - GI: Prior constipation (resolved). No diarrhea reported. Eating and drinking OK. Able to do daily activities but pain is very uncomfortable.
  - GU: Denies problems passing urine; denies pain with urination or strong smell; urinary frequency unclear; drinks a lot of fluids. No flank pain reported.
  - Gyn: Light pink spotting and slight discharge. No heavy bleeding reported.
  - Constitutional/other: Denies fever, feeling feverish, dyspnea, shoulder-tip pain, or presyncope/syncope on standing. No recent travel (last abroad ~1 year ago).
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no shortness of breath, no shoulder pain, no faintness on standing, no known fever.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- Surgical history: No prior surgeries.
- Obstetric/gynecologic: G0 (no prior pregnancies).
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not documented).
- Medications/Devices:
  - Contraceptive implant (Implanon) in situ since ~1 year (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social History:
- Occupation: School teacher.
- Living situation: Lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Tobacco/alcohol: Not clearly documented.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.
- Travel: Last abroad approximately 1 year ago.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (teleconsultation). No vitals available.

Investigations:
- None obtained during this consult.
- Prior: Pregnancy test done about 1 month ago.
- Plan: Home urine pregnancy test today as advised.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain with intermenstrual spotting in a reproductive-age woman on contraceptive implant
  - Assessment: Concerning for gynecologic causes including ectopic pregnancy, PID, or functional ovarian cyst; appendicitis and UTI less likely but not excluded. Worsening constant pain and spotting warrant in-person evaluation. No red flags reported (hemodynamic instability, syncope, shoulder-tip pain), but ectopic pregnancy must be ruled out.
  - Plan:
    - Perform a urine pregnancy test today as instructed. If positive, seek immediate medical evaluation and call back urgently.
    - Arrange face-to-face clinical assessment for abdominal examination (patient agreed to call support line to schedule).
    - Safety net: If pain acutely worsens, if unable to keep fluids down, or if any new red flags (fainting, severe dizziness, heavy bleeding, severe shoulder pain, shortness of breath) occur, seek urgent care/emergency evaluation.
- Issue 2: Nausea without vomiting
  - Assessment: Mild; associated with abdominal pain; maintaining oral intake.
  - Plan: Continue oral fluids as tolerated; seek earlier in-person review if vomiting or inability to maintain hydration develops (per safety net advice).
- Issue 3: Recent constipation, now resolved
  - Assessment: Unlikely to fully explain current persistent/worsening pain.
  - Plan: No specific intervention at present; monitor.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Ectopic pregnancy – Likelihood: Moderate
  - Reasoning: Pelvic pain with light spotting; sexually active; last pregnancy test >1 month ago; contraceptive implant reduces but does not eliminate pregnancy risk; ectopic proportionally higher among pregnancies on implant.
- Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) – Likelihood: Moderate
  - Reasoning: Lower abdominal pain with intermenstrual bleeding and slight discharge in a sexually active patient; absence of fever does not exclude PID.
- Functional/hemorrhagic ovarian cyst (possibly implant-associated) – Likelihood: Moderate
  - Reasoning: Acute pelvic pain with spotting; implant use can be associated with functional cysts. Midline location and non-sudden onset make torsion or rupture less typical but still possible.

Quality checks:
- Missing/expected elements:
  - Vitals, abdominal/pelvic exam findings not available.
  - Urine pregnancy test pending; no urinalysis, STI testing, or imaging documented.
  - Detailed medication list, immunizations, and full allergy reaction details not documented.
  - Detailed sexual history (partners, protection beyond implant, STI history) not documented.
  - Smoking and alcohol use unclear.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Several unclear/noisy segments with partial/inaudible responses; some answers ambiguous (urinary frequency, alcohol/smoking).
